rules.name: Hardcoded Password
rules.description: Detects hardcoded passwords in source code. Passwords should never be stored in code as they can be easily discovered through version control or code inspection.
rules.remediation_hint: Replace hardcoded password with environment variable or secure credential management system (e.g., AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault). Use os.getenv() in Python, process.env in JavaScript.

rules.name: Hardcoded API Key
rules.description: Detects hardcoded API keys, tokens, or secrets in source code. These credentials should be stored securely and never committed to version control.
rules.remediation_hint: Move API keys to environment variables or secure configuration management. Use .env files (excluded from git) or cloud secret managers. Never commit credentials to version control.

rules.name: SQL Injection Vulnerability
rules.description: Detects potential SQL injection vulnerabilities where user input is directly concatenated into SQL queries without proper sanitization or parameterization.
rules.remediation_hint: Use parameterized queries or prepared statements. In Python, use cursor.execute with placeholders (?). In Java, use PreparedStatement. Never concatenate user input directly into SQL queries.
rules.example_violation: cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = " + user_id)

rules.name: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
rules.description: Detects potential XSS vulnerabilities where user input is rendered in HTML without proper escaping or sanitization.
rules.remediation_hint: Always escape user input before rendering in HTML. Use textContent instead of innerHTML for plain text. Use DOMPurify or similar libraries to sanitize HTML. Implement Content Security Policy (CSP).

rules.name: Insecure HTTP Connection
rules.description: Detects use of insecure HTTP protocol for sensitive data transmission. All sensitive data should be transmitted over HTTPS.
rules.remediation_hint: Replace HTTP with HTTPS for all external connections. Ensure SSL/TLS certificates are properly configured. Use HSTS headers to enforce HTTPS.

rules.name: Unmasked Email Address
rules.description: Detects email addresses stored or logged without masking. Under GDPR, personal data like email addresses should be protected and masked in logs.
rules.remediation_hint: Mask email addresses in logs by showing only first character and domain (e.g., j***@example.com). Implement data masking function for PII. Avoid logging personal data unless absolutely necessary.

rules.name: Unencrypted Personal Data Storage
rules.description: Detects storage of personal data without encryption. GDPR requires appropriate security measures including encryption for personal data.
rules.remediation_hint: Encrypt personal data before storage using AES-256 or similar strong encryption. Use database-level encryption or application-level encryption. Implement proper key management.

rules.name: Missing Data Retention Policy
rules.description: Detects data storage without expiration or deletion mechanism. GDPR requires data to be kept only as long as necessary.
rules.remediation_hint: Implement data retention policies with automatic deletion after specified period. Add TTL (Time To Live) to stored data. Create scheduled jobs to purge old data. Document retention periods.

rules.name: Unencrypted PHI Transmission
rules.description: Detects transmission of Protected Health Information (PHI) without encryption. HIPAA requires encryption of PHI in transit.
rules.remediation_hint: Use HTTPS/TLS for all PHI transmission. Implement end-to-end encryption for sensitive health data. Use secure messaging protocols. Ensure minimum TLS 1.2.

rules.name: PHI in Logs
rules.description: Detects logging of Protected Health Information. HIPAA prohibits logging of PHI without proper safeguards and access controls.
rules.remediation_hint: Remove PHI from logs entirely. If logging is necessary, use de-identified data or secure audit logs with access controls. Implement log sanitization to remove sensitive data.

rules.name: Weak Cryptographic Algorithm
rules.description: Detects use of weak or deprecated cryptographic algorithms like MD5, SHA1, or DES that are no longer considered secure.
rules.remediation_hint: Replace weak algorithms with strong alternatives: Use SHA-256 or SHA-3 instead of MD5/SHA1. Use AES-256 instead of DES. Use bcrypt or Argon2 for password hashing.

rules.name: Command Injection
rules.description: Detects potential command injection vulnerabilities where user input is passed to system commands without proper sanitization.
rules.remediation_hint: Never pass user input directly to system commands. Use subprocess with argument lists instead of shell=True. Validate and sanitize all input. Use allowlists for permitted values.

rules.name: Insecure Random Number Generation
rules.description: Detects use of insecure random number generators for security-sensitive operations. Predictable random numbers can compromise security.
rules.remediation_hint: Use cryptographically secure random number generators: secrets module in Python, crypto.randomBytes in Node.js, SecureRandom in Java. Never use standard random for security tokens or cryptographic keys.

rules.name: Bare Exception Handling
rules.description: Detects overly broad exception handling that catches all exceptions, potentially hiding bugs and making debugging difficult.
rules.remediation_hint: Catch specific exceptions only. Handle different exception types appropriately. Log exceptions with full stack traces. Never silently ignore exceptions.

rules.name: Unvalidated Redirect
rules.description: Detects open redirect vulnerabilities where user-controlled input is used in redirects without validation.
rules.remediation_hint: Validate redirect URLs against a whitelist of allowed domains. Use relative URLs when possible. Implement URL validation to prevent open redirects to malicious sites.

rules.name: Credit Card Number Exposure
rules.description: Detects credit card numbers stored or logged without proper masking. PCI-DSS and GDPR require protection of payment card data.
rules.remediation_hint: Never store full credit card numbers. Use tokenization services. Mask all but last 4 digits for display. Comply with PCI-DSS requirements. Use payment gateway APIs.

rules.name: Path Traversal Vulnerability
rules.description: Detects potential path traversal vulnerabilities where user input is used in file paths without proper validation.
rules.remediation_hint: Validate and sanitize file paths. Use os.path.join() or Path() for safe path construction. Implement allowlist of permitted directories. Check for path traversal patterns (.., ./).
rules.example_fix:
from pathlib import Path
safe_path = Path('/var/data').joinpath(filename).resolve()
if safe_path.is_relative_to('/var/data'):
    with open(safe_path) as f:

rules.name: Missing Access Control for PHI
rules.description: Detects access to Protected Health Information without proper authentication or authorization checks.
rules.remediation_hint: Implement role-based access control (RBAC) for all PHI access. Verify user authentication and authorization before granting access. Log all PHI access attempts. Implement audit trails.

rules.name: Insecure Deserialization
rules.description: Detects use of insecure deserialization that can lead to remote code execution vulnerabilities.
rules.remediation_hint: Use safe deserialization methods: yaml.safe_load() instead of yaml.load(), json.loads() instead of pickle. Validate serialized data before deserialization. Never deserialize untrusted data.
rules.example_fix:
import json
data = json.loads(user_input)  # or use yaml.safe_load()

rules.name: Missing Consent Tracking
rules.description: Detects collection of personal data without explicit consent tracking mechanism required by GDPR.
rules.remediation_hint: Implement consent tracking system. Store consent timestamp and type. Provide clear opt-in mechanisms. Allow users to withdraw consent. Document legal basis for data processing.
